opportunities.title: ERDC Broad Agency Announcement
opportunities.summary: This is a technically relevant, continuously open ERDC R&D BAA with an unrestricted applicant classification, but it is not yet a defined pursuit. METSS has evidence-backed adjacency in advanced materials, specialty chemistry and fluids, testing/validation, harsh-environment performance, and pilot-scale transition. The official record, however, provides no specific solicitation topic or submission package from which to establish a scoped work package, full eligibility, prime readiness, or funding fit. Investigate rather than pursue immediately. Timing: the record lists a January 1, 2027 response date and states that pre-proposals are reviewed throughout the year, subject to funding availability.
opportunities.why: ERDC seeks R&D across materials and structures, engineering and environmental processes, hazardous-waste treatment, physical/mechanical/chemical properties, infrastructure, and related military-engineering fields.: The synopsis expressly identifies these fields among ERDC's broad research areas and states that pre-proposals are sought for all identified research areas. (Official Grants.gov record) METSS has public capabilities relevant to potential ERDC materials, chemistry, environmental-process, and testing concepts.: The profile documents advanced materials; physical, organic, inorganic, and analytical chemistry; functional fluids; product/process development; chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, and materials-compatibility testing; and pilot-scale/light-manufacturing capability. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has public past-performance examples that provide subject-matter adjacency for materials, fluids, chemical survivability, and domestic critical-chemical work.: Public examples include Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials, Lubricating Oil Study, Vapor Purge and Chemical Agent Persistence in Aircraft, Aircraft and Sensitive Equipment CBRN Survivability Capability Development and Transition, and DPA Title III Critical Chemicals Production. (Approved METSS public profile) The opportunity is structurally open to a broad applicant population and remains open for pre-proposals during the stated announcement period.: Applicant type is listed as unrestricted; additional eligibility is blank; the synopsis states the announcement is continuously open and that pre-proposals may be submitted and reviewed throughout the year. The listed response date is January 1, 2027. (Official Grants.gov record)
opportunities.action: Retrieve and review the current ERDCWERX BAA materials referenced by the Official Grants.gov record, identify an active research area with a concrete METSS-led materials/chemistry/testing concept, and then verify METSS registration, submission, resource, and cooperative-agreement requirements before selecting prime or partner role.

opportunities.title: ARMY APPLICATIONS LAB BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT FOR DISRUPTIVE APPLICATIONS
opportunities.agency: Dept of the Army -- Materiel Command
opportunities.type: Cooperative Agreement / Grant / Other / Procurement Contract
opportunities.summary: This is a technically adjacent, continuously open Army applied-research BAA rather than a defined procurement requirement. METSS has evidence-backed relevance for a narrowly framed protection, chemical/materials, CBRN survivability, decontamination, harsh-environment, testing/validation, or domestic scale-up concept. The record does not prove that such a topic is currently funded or sought, nor does it establish METSS's administrative and instrument-specific eligibility. Investigation is warranted before committing bid and proposal resources; a generic response based only on broad Army modernization keywords should not be pursued.
opportunities.why: The BAA seeks basic and applied research, early-stage technology demonstrations, translational research, and dual-use commercialization supporting Army modernization and future-force needs.: Pages 6–10 describe AAL discovery, acceleration, translation, disruptive-innovation, dual-use, and continuously open research structure. (AAL BAA W911NF-24-S-0008.pdf) The BAA expressly includes protection, contested logistics, sensing, power and energy, signature reduction, and related materials-science-relevant disciplines among its areas of interest.: Pages 11–16 identify the Army modernization technical areas; pages 20–21 identify chemistry, life sciences, materials science, mechanical sciences, and environmental sciences as eligible scientific disciplines. (AAL BAA W911NF-24-S-0008.pdf) METSS has public capabilities potentially applicable to a protection-focused or materials/chemistry-based applied-R&D concept, including chemical-protective materials, polymers, coatings, adhesives, harsh-environment materials, formulation, and product development.: The Advanced materials and Chemistry and functional fluids capability sections describe chemical-protective materials, polymers, coatings, adhesives, specialty chemistry, harsh-environment materials, formulation, sample analysis, and product development. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has public testing, CBRN, and survivability capabilities that could support an evidence-backed research work package if a current AAL topic accepts such a concept.: The Testing and validation and Microbiology and CBRN capability sections identify compatibility, environmental, performance, chemical and biological field testing, decontamination evaluation, agent persistence, and sensitive-equipment survivability work. (Approved METSS public profile)
opportunities.action: Check the current AAL website for active ongoing or special topics and request/identify the appropriate AAL technical contact. Proceed only if a current topic supports a concrete METSS-led applied-R&D concept with a defensible Army use case and measurable disruptive improvement. In parallel, obtain internal verification of SAM/UEI status, intended prime/subcontract posture, resource availability, budget/indirect-rate readiness, disclosure information, and any export-control or security constraints before submitting a whitepaper.
opportunities.eligibility: CONDITIONAL: METSS Corporation is a for-profit organization, a permitted applicant category under the BAA. However, eligibility for submission and award remains conditional because the reviewed materials require an active SAM registration and valid UEI, and may require recipient-qualification, contractor-responsibility, disclosure, export-control, security, and instrument-specific determinations. The approved METSS public profile does not establish these items. title_iii_relevance.rationale: The BAA is not identified as a DPA Title III solicitation and does not specifically seek critical-chemical production. It is strategically adjacent to METSS's public DPA Title III and domestic-industrial-base priorities because it seeks disruptive applied R&D, technology translation, dual-use commercialization, and may support prototyping or transition. A Title III production work package is not evidenced by the reviewed BAA.

evidence.claim: The BAA seeks basic and applied research, early-stage technology demonstrations, translational research, and dual-use commercialization supporting Army modernization and future-force needs.
evidence.support: Pages 6–10 describe AAL discovery, acceleration, translation, disruptive-innovation, dual-use, and continuously open research structure.

evidence.claim: The BAA expressly includes protection, contested logistics, sensing, power and energy, signature reduction, and related materials-science-relevant disciplines among its areas of interest.
evidence.support: Pages 11–16 identify the Army modernization technical areas; pages 20–21 identify chemistry, life sciences, materials science, mechanical sciences, and environmental sciences as eligible scientific disciplines.

evidence.claim: METSS has public capabilities potentially applicable to a protection-focused or materials/chemistry-based applied-R&D concept, including chemical-protective materials, polymers, coatings, adhesives, harsh-environment materials, formulation, and product development.

evidence.claim: For-profit organizations, including large and small businesses, are eligible applicants, but SAM/UEI and award-qualification requirements apply.

evidence.claim: The normal submission path requires a whitepaper or qualifying demonstration presentation before a full proposal; current topics and funding availability must be checked through AAL channels.
evidence.support: Pages 21–26 establish the preliminary whitepaper/qualifying-demonstration process and AAL website submission; pages 6–10 state the continuously open structure and that topics are subject to relevance and funding availability.

gaps: The BAA is broad, and no supplied current AAL ongoing topic or special topic specifically requests chemical-protective materials, CBRN survivability, decontamination, functional fluids, critical chemicals, or METSS's other public capability areas.

A concept must demonstrate the BAA's stated disruptive improvement standard, approximately 2–4 times improvement over current or planned Army capabilities; no METSS-specific performance evidence supporting that threshold was supplied.

METSS public profile does not establish active SAM registration, UEI, representations, responsibility status, available personnel, facility/equipment capacity, schedule availability, indirect rates, proposal budget, or cost-sharing capacity.
The specific award instrument, funding amount, award duration, Government technical sponsor, and current funding availability are unknown.
The profile does not establish export-control registrations, clearances, CMMC status, or the ability to perform any classified or CUI-restricted requirement, should such requirements arise.
No publicly supported METSS concept, technical objectives, Army use case, current/end-state TRL, milestones, schedule, or cost estimate has been provided for the required whitepaper.
partner_needs: No partner is presently required for a plausible METSS prime whitepaper focused on materials, chemistry, CBRN/decontamination, testing, or scale-up research.

If the selected current topic requires autonomy, AI/ML, networking, sensing hardware, PNT, quantum, space, or other areas not evidenced in the METSS profile, a qualified technical partner would be needed or METSS should decline that topic.

If a proposed effort requires specialized Army operational validation, classified/CUI access, human-subjects work, animal research, or resources beyond METSS's confirmed public facilities, identify an appropriately qualified partner only after verifying the requirement and METSS's role.
